questions.question: Which observation is part of the general survey?
choices: Work of breathing, appearance, mobility, speech, and level of distress
Only the patient’s BMI
Only the medication list
Only a laboratory result
questions.explanation: The general survey begins before the formal examination and provides immediate information about stability, function, and urgency.

questions.question: Why is functional impact important in the HPI?
choices: It can reveal severity and change from baseline even when a patient minimizes symptoms
It replaces the physical examination
It is relevant only for older adults
It is unrelated to diagnostic reasoning
questions.explanation: New inability to walk, work, sleep, eat, or perform usual activities may be a key indicator of illness severity and should be compared with baseline.

questions.question: What is the safest medication-reconciliation practice?
choices: Copy the medication list from the prior visit
Ask about the exact name, dose, route, schedule, indication, actual use, OTC products, supplements, and recent changes
Review prescription medications only
Assume patients use medications exactly as prescribed
questions.explanation: Complete reconciliation is diagnostic and prescribing safety work. Chart lists may omit duplicate products, nonprescription agents, cost-related nonadherence, and misunderstanding.

questions.question: A patient has an unexpectedly high office blood pressure. What is the best first step before making a chronic treatment decision?
choices: Verify technique and repeat the measurement in clinical context
Diagnose chronic hypertension from one reading
Ignore the value if the patient looks comfortable
Immediately add multiple medications without assessment
questions.explanation: Blood pressure can be affected by technique, position, cuff size, activity, caffeine, pain, anxiety, and other factors. Repeat concerning values correctly and assess the whole clinical picture.

questions.question: Which blood-pressure technique supports a more accurate reading?
choices: Cuff over clothing with legs crossed
Patient talking while the arm hangs below heart level
Back supported, feet flat and uncrossed, arm supported at heart level, correct cuff on bare skin, and no talking
Measure immediately after exercise without rest
questions.explanation: Correct positioning, cuff placement/size, rest, and avoidance of talking reduce measurement error and support sound clinical decisions.

questions.question: When are orthostatic vital signs most useful?
choices: For every asymptomatic annual visit
For selected patients with dizziness, syncope/presyncope, falls, suspected volume loss, medication effects, or postural symptoms
To replace emergency assessment in an unstable patient
Only to diagnose one specific disease
questions.explanation: Orthostatic measurements are selective tools. They may help with postural symptoms or volume risk but must be interpreted with the full clinical context.

questions.question: Which patient should not be asked to stand simply to complete orthostatic vital signs?
choices: A stable patient with mild positional dizziness who can stand safely
A patient with active major bleeding, severe hypotension, or inability to stand safely
A patient with a normal gait and no symptoms
A patient who has had a blood pressure measurement before
questions.explanation: Do not create a fall risk or delay stabilization. High-risk symptoms and instability require urgent/emergency assessment rather than routine orthostatic testing.

questions.question: A patient has severe dyspnea, cyanosis, confusion, and cannot speak in full sentences. What is the FNP priority?
choices: Complete every element of the social history first
Recognize possible airway/breathing/circulation compromise and arrange immediate emergency evaluation
Schedule routine pulmonary testing next month
Focus only on a normal pulse oximeter reading
questions.explanation: Visible respiratory distress and altered mental status are emergency red flags. Stabilization and appropriate transfer take priority over a prolonged outpatient assessment.

questions.question: Which statement about pulse oximetry is most accurate?
choices: A normal value rules out all serious respiratory disease
It should be interpreted with signal quality, perfusion, work of breathing, mental status, and clinical trend
A low value should never be repeated
It eliminates the need for a respiratory examination
questions.explanation: Pulse oximetry is useful but has limitations. Clinical condition and measurement quality matter, and visible distress can be serious even with a seemingly reassuring number.

questions.question: What is an essential element of a safe outpatient assessment plan?
choices: Vague advice to return if worse
Documented follow-up ownership, pending-result plan, and specific urgent/emergency return precautions
Avoiding discussion of uncertainty
Copying forward a prior normal examination
questions.explanation: Diagnostic safety requires clear follow-up and explicit return precautions, not merely a completed visit note.
